overview.problemStatement: Inbound provider webhooks arrive at an HTTP edge that must survive a restart, and the four guarantees that matter - the signature is genuine, the event is not a replay, the same delivery is not processed twice, and a verified event is not lost between verification and handling - all require durable state that a per-provider client cannot own. wirekit verifies signatures for the providers it wraps, but it holds no delivery record, no replay window, and no outbox, so every edge service re-implements dedupe and retry slightly differently and loses an event the first time it crashes mid-delivery.
overview.proposedSolution: Port and adapt the hookgate crate from feature/m3-substrate as prior art: DeliveryId, IdempotencyKey, InboundRequest, VerifiedEvent, DeliveryRecord, InsertOutcome, DeadLetterRecord, and the Verifier, DeliveryStore, and Outbox traits, plus a redacting error type and provider verifier presets. Establish the load-bearing rule that verification runs over the exact received bytes and never over a re-serialization. Ship MemoryDeliveryStore for tests and single-process callers, and verifier presets for Meta, Stripe, Shopify, Twilio, Slack, GitHub, and a configurable generic HMAC. No axum integration, no SendGrid ECDSA verifier, and no standalone binary in 0.1.
overview.targetAudience: Rust teams running a webhook ingress edge, and this project's service layer that now receives every provider's events.
assumptions: A working implementation exists on feature/m3-substrate (20 files, features default and presets) and is ported and adapted rather than redesigned.
main has no [workspace.dependencies], and the branch manifests use *.workspace = true, so every dependency is declared directly in the crate manifest.
The contract is at-least-once delivery with idempotent handlers, not exactly-once; this is documented rather than implied.
The branch tests are not ported; the test agent authors tests against this specification.
The unmerged m3-substrate/v1 spec covers four crates and is not reused as governance here.
outOfScope: A provider client and any outbound HTTP.
An HTTP server or axum integration in 0.1.
A queue implementation; the Outbox trait writes to the caller's choice of queue.
Domain handling of any event type; hookgate does not know what an event means.
Tenant resolution and authentication; the caller supplies the tenant.

userStories.title: Verify a signature over the raw bytes
userStories.want: to verify a provider signature against the exact received body
userStories.benefit: a tampered or re-serialized payload is rejected rather than trusted

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given an InboundRequest carrying raw body bytes, when a Verifier::verify runs, then it computes the signature over those exact bytes and never over a re-serialization of parsed parameters.
Given a valid signature, when verify runs, then it returns a VerifiedEvent carrying the provider, delivery id, event id if present, event type, parsed payload, and the raw bytes.

userStories.title: Reject tampered and stale requests
userStories.benefit: an attacker cannot forge or replay a webhook

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a body whose bytes were changed after signing, when verify runs, then it fails with a typed verification error and no event is produced.
Given a valid signature whose timestamp is outside the allowed skew, when verify runs, then it is rejected as stale rather than accepted.

userStories.title: Deduplicate deliveries
userStories.benefit: a provider retry does not double-apply an event

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a delivery already stored for a provider and event id, when it is inserted again, then the outcome is Duplicate rather than a second insert.
Given the same event id arriving for two different tenants, when both are stored, then they are not duplicates of each other because the uniqueness key includes the tenant.

userStories.title: Hand off through an outbox
userStories.want: a verified event persisted and enqueued before acknowledging
userStories.benefit: a crash between verification and handling does not lose the event

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a new verified event, when it is accepted, then the delivery record and the outbox entry are written before success is reported, so a crash afterwards leaves the event recoverable.
Given a stored delivery, when it is marked processed or failed, then the terminal state is recorded and a failure can be dead-lettered with its error and raw body.

userStories.title: Replay a dead-lettered delivery
userStories.want: to inspect and replay a failed delivery
userStories.benefit: a poison message is recoverable instead of lost

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a dead-lettered record, when it is read, then the raw body and the failure reason are available, and replaying it is idempotent against the delivery store.

userStories.title: Ship provider verifier presets
userStories.want: correct verifiers for the common providers
userStories.benefit: I do not re-implement each provider's signature quirk

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the presets feature, when it is enabled, then verifiers are provided for Meta, Stripe, Shopify, Twilio, Slack, and GitHub, and a configurable generic HMAC verifier covers an unlisted provider.
Given the crate built without the presets feature, when it compiles, then the core types, traits, and memory store are present and the preset verifiers are absent.

userStories.title: Isolate tenants and never leak secrets
userStories.benefit: one tenant's delivery cannot be read by another and no secret reaches a log

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a stored delivery, when it is read, then the tenant scoping prevents another tenant from reading it.
Given a verification or store failure, when it is formatted and logged, then the error is redacted and carries no secret material such as a signature or a shared secret.
Given the crate, when it is built with all features on Rust 1.87, then it compiles with forbid(unsafe_code) and deny(missing_docs) and ships the licence files.

functionalRequirements.text: The crate MUST expose DeliveryId, IdempotencyKey, InboundRequest, VerifiedEvent, DeliveryRecord, InsertOutcome, DeadLetterRecord, and the Verifier, DeliveryStore, and Outbox traits per catalogue/30_webhook_gateway.md.
Verification MUST operate on the raw received bytes and MUST NOT re-serialize the body before verifying (CON-215).
Verification MUST be constant-time and MUST fail closed on a mismatch.
A timestamp tolerance MUST be enforced and a request outside it MUST be rejected as stale.
DeliveryStore MUST provide insert_if_new returning an outcome, mark_processed, and mark_failed, and insert_if_new MUST be idempotent per tenant and event id.
The delivery and outbox writes for a new event MUST complete before success is reported.
A failed delivery MUST be recordable as dead-lettered with its error and raw body, and MUST be replayable idempotently.
A presets feature MUST ship verifiers for Meta, Stripe, Shopify, Twilio, Slack, and GitHub plus a configurable generic HMAC verifier, and MUST be absent when the feature is off.
The crate MUST NOT contain a provider client, an outbound HTTP call, an HTTP server, or an axum integration.
Errors MUST be redacted and MUST NOT expose a signature, a secret, or raw credential material.
The crate MUST declare forbid(unsafe_code) and deny(missing_docs).

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Every delivery read and write MUST be scoped by tenant, so no tenant can observe another's delivery (CON-512).
Stored secrets and signature material MUST be redacted in Debug, Display, logs, and error payloads (CON-214).
Untrusted input - headers, raw body, and event ids - MUST be validated and bounded before use, and an oversized or malformed request MUST produce a typed error rather than a panic (CON-515).
The crate MUST NOT read secrets from the environment; the caller supplies the verifier's secret (CON-519).
The crate MUST compile on Rust 1.87 with all features and MUST contain no product vocabulary (CON-102, CON-106).
Every public item MUST carry rustdoc and every module MUST state its scope and non-goals (CON-202, CON-203).

edgeCases.description: A JSON body is parsed and re-serialized before verification
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Verification fails, because the canonical string no longer matches the received bytes.

edgeCases.description: The same event id arrives from two tenants
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Both are stored; they are not duplicates because the uniqueness key includes the tenant.

edgeCases.description: Crash after insert but before outbox enqueue
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The contract requires both to commit before success; a partial write must be detectable and replayable.

edgeCases.description: An unlisted provider with a custom HMAC header and prefix
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The generic verifier accepts the caller's header name, encoding, and prefix.

edgeCases.description: A poison delivery that always fails handling
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: It is dead-lettered with its raw body rather than blocking the outbox forever.
Core compiles; no preset verifier is present.

risks.description: The raw-body rule is easy to violate accidentally by a well-meaning refactor that parses first, which silently breaks every signature.
risks.mitigation: AC-001 and AC-003 assert it directly, and EC-001 names the failure so a test can pin it.

risks.description: The delivery-and-outbox-before-acknowledge guarantee is weak when the two writes are not transactional in the memory store.
risks.mitigation: State the guarantee explicitly for the store contract and pin it with AC-007 and EC-003.

risks.description: Porting stale code may drag in manifests using workspace inheritance the current workspace does not define, and the branch dev-depends on quota-ledger.
risks.mitigation: Adapt the manifest to declare dependencies directly and drop the cross-crate dev-dependency unless the test needs it.
